steps.body: A journey's total distance collects every leg: add them one at a time and let the running total walk with you.
steps.narration: A journey's total distance collects every leg: add them one at a time and let the running total walk with you.

widget.prompt: Legs of a hike: the first two banked 55 m; the last leg is 20 m. Hop its tens.

commonLandings.feedback: Two meters of the last leg — the full 20 belongs in the total.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 55, 2 hops land on 75.
widget.successFeedback: 75 meters — every leg collected, no meter walked twice.

predict.prompt: A total distance skips one leg. Is it still the total?
predict.reveal: Leaving out a leg measures a different, shorter journey — the total owes every part its due.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2p total distance.
invariants: Lengths compare only from a shared start, join by placing end to end, and split so the parts rebuild the whole exactly for g2p total distance.
misconceptions: Comparing unaligned ends, reading a ruler's end mark as a length, or letting a total drift from the sum of its parts.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What would have to change about the pieces for the total or the gap to come out differently?

widget.prompt: 34 + 20 = ? (the third leg joins the first two legs of 23 m, 11 m, and 20 m)

commonErrors.feedback: The third leg never joined — a total distance collects EVERY leg walked.
The last leg was counted twice; each leg enters the total once.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Line the lengths up: same starting point, then read what the ends say — joins add, gaps subtract.

hints: Place the pieces end to end.
The total is the far end.

widget.prompt: Maggie computes that a pencil measured from the 3 cm mark to the 11 cm mark is 14 cm long. Reasonable?

options.label: Too long — the marks are only 8 apart
options.feedback: Correct — 11 − 3 = 8, so 14 overshoots; she likely added the marks instead of subtracting.

options.label: Reasonable — rulers can stretch
options.feedback: A ruler's spacing is fixed by design; the span between 3 and 11 can only ever be 8.

options.label: Too short
options.feedback: The error runs the other way — 14 is LARGER than the true 8 cm span.

options.label: Impossible to judge without the pencil
options.feedback: The two marks alone pin the length; the marks ARE the measurement.
